newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss lower house approves core of stimulus plan.
newsitem.headline: Swiss lower house approves core of stimulus plan.

text.p: The lower house of Switzerland's parliament approved key portions of the government's economic stimulus package during a special session called to deal with the moribund economy.
The upper house approved the measures on Monday. Minor differences between the two versions must still be worked out.

Berne says its plan to put up 561 million francs in matching funds could generate 2.4 billion in new infrastructure spending, add a third of a percentage point in gross domestic product growth in 1998 and 1999 and create some 24,000 jobs.
A final vote on the entire package was expected on Wednesday. Passage was virtually assured, although analysts have questioned whether the programme would have much impact on growth or employment.
The lower house approved one measure on upgrading state roads by a 104-19 margin. It approved a second measure on other infrastructure projects by 128 to 28.
Other smaller parts of the package still had to be voted on.
